text.brief: In October 1998 Michael Eisner apologized to Premier Zhu Rongji for Disney's release of Kundun.
text.record: Martin Scorsese's film about the Dalai Lama's youth had drawn warnings from Party officials before its release in December 1997. Disney released it in a small number of theaters, and the Party froze Disney's business on the mainland. Disney hired Henry Kissinger's consulting firm to repair the relationship, and Eisner's apology followed.
text.reading: The Party punished one film to warn a whole industry, which is Stratagem 26. The studios learned the lesson and began to cut scripts before the Party needed to ask, as PEN America documented in 2020.
text.gapText: Business Architecture. Each studio weighed its own market access alone, so no film carried the industry's collective interest.
text.fix: Disclose every change made to a film for a foreign censor, so audiences and regulators can see the price of access.
